case_title: Roy Fernandes v. State of Goa and Ors.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of offences punishable under Sections 143, 148, 323, 325 and 302 read with Section 149
high_court_outcome: Upheld conviction of appellant and accused no.2, set aside conviction of other three
neutral_facts: The accused, a man in his 60s, was involved in a dispute with the victim, a man also in his 60s, over the use of a path near the victim's house. The victim and his companions were attempting to put up a fence around a chapel property when the victim's daughter raised an objection. A van arrived carrying five individuals, including the accused, who intervened. The accused pushed and slapped the victim, causing him to fall. Another accused, who was carrying a knife, stabbed the victim in the thigh, leading to his death. The prosecution alleged that the accused had a common object of preventing the fence from being put up, but the court found no evidence of this. The accused was acquitted of murder but convicted of lesser offenses.
